hypothesis: Dynamic int8 quantization of the two post-route-selection task-cake projections is the remaining reasoning bottleneck. Keeping only those two sparse projections in float32 will recover route-cake behavior while the shared transformer, embeddings, and output projection remain int8 and the graph still activates one task cake.

implementation.note: The hash binds the implementation after adding the isolated precision path and before any successor export.

validation_order: Export the exact v24 checkpoint while excluding only the two graph-discovered route-selected task-cake MatMul nodes from dynamic quantization.
Require identity PASS and graph-level physical sparse PASS, including proof that both declared float32 MatMuls consume weights only after route selection.
Run the full adaptively reused broad14 CPU suite and require every locked semantic gate.
Only if broad14 passes, run the locked CPU speed, TTFT, RSS, persistent-state, paired-teacher, and other non-final gates on this exact graph.
Do not access or generate final evidence unless every non-final gate passes.
decision_rule: Reject the hybrid runtime if reasoning remains below 0.80, any other capability falls below 0.80, collapse is nonzero, retention falls below 0.90, physical sparsity or identity fails, or later CPU throughput falls below 2x the optimized transformer. Do not perform another nearby precision split.
claim_boundary: This is one bounded runtime precision-isolation experiment, not a training change or quality claim. It may promote only if the same exact graph clears every product gate.
